Let <MATH_0001> be a finite <ACCENT_0001>tale morphism of schemes. Let <MATH_0002> be a
Noetherian ring. If <MATH_0003> is a constructible sheaf of sets,
constructible sheaf of abelian groups, or constructible sheaf of
<MATH_0004>-modules on <MATH_0005>, the same is true for
<MATH_0006> on <MATH_0007>.

By Lemma <REF_0001> it suffices to check this
Zariski locally on <MATH_0001> and by Lemma <REF_0002>
we may replace <MATH_0002> by an <ACCENT_0001>tale cover (the construction of <MATH_0003>
commutes with <ACCENT_0002>tale localization). A finite <ACCENT_0003>tale morphism is
<ACCENT_0004>tale locally isomorphic to a disjoint union of isomorphisms, see
<ACCENT_0005>tale Morphisms, Lemma <REF_0003>.
Thus, in the case of sheaves of sets, the lemma says that if
<MATH_0004>, <MATH_0005> are constructible sheaves of sets, then
<MATH_0006> is too.
This is clear. Similarly for sheaves of abelian groups and modules.

Let <MATH_0001> be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme. The category of
constructible sheaves of sets is the full subcategory of <MATH_0002>
consisting of sheaves <MATH_0003> which are coequalizers
<MATH_0004>
such that <MATH_0005>, <MATH_0006> is a finite coproduct of sheaves of
the form <MATH_0007> with <MATH_0008> a quasi-compact and quasi-separated
object of <MATH_0009>.

In the proof of Lemma <REF_0001>
we have seen that sheaves of this form are constructible.
For the converse, suppose that for every constructible sheaf of
sets <MATH_0001> we can find a surjection <MATH_0002>
with <MATH_0003> as in the lemma. Then we find our surjection
<MATH_0004>
because the latter is constructible by Lemma <REF_0002>.
